answer: Sustained Timing Skew Admission. Each identity must send its first 50 messages interleaved with idle gaps drawn from a fixed distribution, measured as a pulse of activity rather than a burst. An agent whose arrival timestamps cluster too tightly (cross-identity timber similarity) is throttled until the gaps widen. Because attackers must hold each fake identity idle for the full ramp period, the per-identity cost is wall-clock time and lost throughput across the whole grove of accounts, not a one-time fee.
